notes: Fiscal-year label mapping: schema year 2023 corresponds to Ulta fiscal year ended Feb 3, 2024; year 2024 corresponds to fiscal year ended Feb 1, 2025; year 2025 corresponds to fiscal year ended Jan 31, 2026. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001558370-25-003810/ulta-20250201x10k.htm))
EBIT is modeled as GAAP Operating income (not adjusted operating income). ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001558370-25-003810/ulta-20250201x10k.htm))

NWC definition (for historical NWC and forecast NWC as % sales): NWC = (Receivables, net + Merchandise inventories, net + Prepaid expenses and other current assets + Prepaid income taxes) − (Accounts payable + Accrued liabilities + Deferred revenue + Accrued income taxes). This excludes cash/short-term investments, short-term debt, and current operating lease liabilities to keep NWC tied to operating working capital rather than financing/lease structure. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001558370-25-003810/ulta-20250201x10k.htm))

FY2025 values come from the company’s FY2025 results press release (unaudited) rather than a 10-K in this run; final audited numbers may differ. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Tax rate uses an effective tax rate implied by company-reported GAAP income tax expense divided by pre-tax income for FY2023–FY2025, averaged to form a stable DCF input (analytical choice). ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001558370-25-003810/ulta-20250201x10k.htm))
WACC, terminal growth, and terminal method are analytical DCF inputs (not explicitly disclosed by Ulta) set for economic sensibility; adjust in your model governance as needed.

Comps NTM multiple fields (EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, P/E NTM) were not populated due to lack of consistently retrievable NTM multiple inputs from primary/official sources in this run; fields left null by design.

NOL balance and utilization percent were not populated as numerically reliable DCF inputs because Ulta discloses NOL-related tax attributes, but the NOL tax-basis/use rate needed for a utilization assumption was not unambiguously available for this package. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0001558370-25-003810/ulta-20250201x10k.htm))

catalysts: Outperformance (or miss) vs FY2026 net sales growth and comparable sales ranges; impacts near-term earnings power. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Operating leverage: continued improvement in gross margin/opex discipline leading to faster EBIT margin normalization vs base case. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Execution of international initiatives (including Space NK) and integration-related synergy realization. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
company_overview: Largest U.S. specialty beauty retailer with a large assortment across cosmetics, fragrance, skin care, hair care, wellness, and salon services. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Omnichannel model: store base plus e-commerce/app, supported by Ulta Beauty Rewards loyalty engagement. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

International growth via Space NK (U.K. & Ireland) and other international initiatives (including joint venture/franchise structure). ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
current_context: Fiscal 2025 (ended Jan 31, 2026) net sales of $12.39B (+9.7% YoY) and operating income of $1.53B (12.4% of net sales). ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Balance sheet/capital deployment: cash & cash equivalents of $424M, short-term investments of $70M, and short-term debt of $62M; invested $435M in capital expenditures during fiscal 2025. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Fiscal 2026 outlook: net sales growth guidance of 6.0% to 7.0% and capital expenditures of $400M to $450M. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes continued mid-to-high single-digit top-line growth supported by new store openings and improving comparable sales, consistent with FY2026 guidance. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

EBIT margin modeled as gradual mean reversion from FY2025 levels toward a normalized low-to-mid-13% profile as strategic investments mature. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Capital intensity kept steady (capex modeled in the ~3.3% to ~3.5% of sales range) to match recent capex levels and FY2026 capex guidance. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Working-capital needs normalized around ~6.6% to ~6.9% of sales based on recent NWC history derived from operating balance-sheet components. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
Valuation anchors combine a DCF with a comps cross-check (comps multiples left null where consistent NTM inputs were not retrievable in this run).
key_risks: Consumer demand volatility and promotional intensity could pressure comparable sales and merchandise margin. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Investment/expense acceleration (e.g., technology, corporate overhead, marketing) may delay margin recovery. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))

Working-capital swings (inventory build/turns and payables) could reduce free cash flow relative to DCF assumptions. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
Modeling risk: WACC and terminal assumptions are not explicitly disclosed by the company and are set as analytical inputs.

valuation_summary: DCF drivers are chained from FY2025 revenue and built from empirically observed operating relationships (EBIT margin, D&A intensity, capex intensity, and working-capital intensity) using primary-company disclosures. ([ulta.com](https://www.ulta.com/investor/news-events/press-releases/detail/224/ulta-beauty-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025))
Terminal value uses a Gordon-growth framework with a conservative terminal growth assumption reflecting long-run mature retail economics (modeled, not explicitly disclosed).
Scenario framing (bull/bear) adjusts only a few key levers—growth, EBIT margin, WACC, and terminal growth—while keeping operating cost structure and reinvestment intensity broadly consistent.
